name: Paracetamol
summary: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) is an analgesic and antipyretic used to treat fever and mild to moderate pain. Excessive amounts can cause severe liver injury.
metabolism: Evidence is from Alvedon suppositories 60 mg, 125 mg and 250 mg (rectal). Paracetamol is well absorbed by both oral and rectal routes, with peak plasma concentrations about 2 to 3 hours after rectal administration and a plasma half-life of about 2 hours. Paracetamol is primarily metabolised in the liver by conjugation to glucuronide and sulphate. A small amount, about 3-10% of a therapeutic dose, is metabolised by oxidation, and the reactive intermediate metabolite thus formed is bound preferentially to liver glutathione and excreted as cystein and mercapturic acid conjugates. Excretion occurs via the kidneys: 2-3% of a therapeutic dose is excreted unchanged, 80-90% as glucuronide and sulphate, and a smaller amount as cystein and mercapturic acid derivatives.
